Speculative decoding is an inference‑time acceleration technique for autoregressive transformers. Below is a detailed technical treatment.

## 1. Problem Setting

A standard decoder‑only LLM generates tokens one at a time:
- At step t it computes logits over the vocabulary V via a single forward pass.
- It then samples (or argmaxes) the next token.
- To produce n tokens, it runs n sequential forward passes.

Each forward pass is memory‑bandwidth bound on modern accelerators (weights must be streamed from HBM to compute units). For a model with P parameters and batch size 1, the arithmetic intensity (FLOPs / bytes) of one token is roughly:

  A ≈ 2P / (2P) = 1 FLOP/byte (plus activation traffic)

This is far below the roofline of GPUs/TPUs (hundreds of FLOP/byte). Hence the GPU is idle much of the time; latency per token is dominated by memory bandwidth, not FLOPs.

Speculative decoding changes the workload so the same bandwidth budget is used to check many candidate tokens in one pass, increasing arithmetic intensity and reducing wall‑clock latency per accepted token.
